Traced through coordinator.ts's commit()/invalidate()/unitExecution()/exchange() logic against the five new/changed tests (subject-monitor.test.ts's six cases, controller.test.ts's updated boundary-invalidation case, coordinator.test.ts's mutation case, and subject.test.ts's identity/containment assertions): every race the tests exercise (blocked native call outliving invalidation, late controller plan/result racing a delayed activity save, subject change racing the final-report commit, invalidation-persistence itself failing) resolves to the correct terminal state — no late output is ever accepted, restoring the original bytes never revives an aborted job (the sticky AbortController, not a live re-check, is what gates re-entry), and unrelated file changes in the same directory (or outside the repo-relative subject paths) never trigger invalidation. progress.ts's new report-suppression line (`report=...` gated to passed/changes_requested/incomplete) correctly hides a stale report once status flips to invalidated/failed, even though the underlying attempt.report field is intentionally left untouched by invalidate() (consistent with checkpoint.ts's immutable-history rule that a sealed report can never be replaced). The code follows the file's existing extremely-dense style and naming conventions; no scope creep beyond S2's subject-invalidation requirement was found.
